items.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025
items.q: maybe throw in a Johnny Cash thing

ctx.x: Well the question I had in mind works either way. When someone calls you, do they ask for a specific thing you do, or do they say, “We’d like to book you” and do you have to say, “well which Dave Bennett do you want?”

In essence, I mean I would say within the last three or four years the audiences that I play for aren’t quite as purist in either direction you know. I’m finding that if I perform the shows where there’s a variety of things in one show that seems to be the most powerful impact I’ve noticed. So for instance my quartet, which is what I tour with most of the time, I’m on clarinet probably sixty to seventy percent of the show. And then I’ll pick up the guitar and play a few things that I’ve written, to kind of…

know. I mean I don’t think things are too stylistically different that it would be too much of a change. But you know I’ll start off the show — we usually open up with our version of “Eleanor Rigby” on the clarinet and it’s kind of a — it’s — we’ve kind of turned it into a jazzy, pop, funky thing. But it’s not far out but it really has a nice groove to it. So that gets people drawn in. And then I’ll do a few things of my own, and then keep mixing in new and old stuff. And then at the end of the show I’ll go to…
